_read_me: THE ONE PLACE for how appointments get handed out: rep roster and hours (set on the board's Reps tab), ratings, daily and weekly limits, lanes, and when rules can bend. Nothing else in the repo repeats these numbers. When the dashboard's Reps & Availability tab is live, it will own the 'roster' section and this file's roster becomes its saved copy.

roster._read_me: One entry per rep, name exactly as in AccuLynx. week: day -> [earliest appt, last appt, home by or null]; a missing day = off. start_date = first day at Rapid (Hero's Journey Day 1). lane: regular, specialty (also runs regular), commercial (commercial/flat only, plus specialty backup).

office._note: Bohemia. On these days reps leave from the office, other days from home.

ratings._read_me: Ratings update every run from the certified close rate on the rolling 30 (rolling 90 if the rep has fewer than 10 sits in the last 30). Reps in their first 90 days are New no matter what.

Lane._note: Reps on the commercial lane: commercial work, plus specialty backup.

hero_journey._read_me: New reps, from start_date (Day 1). Matches the Hero's Journey onboarding tracker.
hero_journey.below_checkpoint: Capped at 7 with no minimum; flagged for management review.

yearly_promise._note: 7 a week on average over a rolling quarter for a fully open schedule. Reps who limit their days or hours get a promise scaled to what they make available. Reps behind their own promise get a nudge on close calls.

full_schedule._read_me: What a fully open schedule is: works 11 of every 14 days (weekends included) and can take appointments across the usual hours. typical_time_share = share of past appointment start times a standard 10 AM to 7 PM day covers. A rep with fewer days or a home-by time gets a promise cut by the share of days and appointment times he can't take.

weekly_order._read_me: Money first. Every appointment goes to the rep most likely to close it, inside hours, daily limits and caps. Minimums are a promise over a rolling quarter, not each week: a small credit nudges close calls toward reps behind their 7-a-week average over the last quarter, and toward a rep's weekly number, but never outweighs a real close-chance gap. Appointments keep coming in all week, so a light week now fills later.

lanes.commercial: Commercial work goes only to reps on the commercial lane. If none can take it: Nobody free, for the sales manager.
lanes.specialty: Specialty work goes to reps on the specialty lane first, commercial-lane reps as backup.
lanes.regular: Regular work goes to regular and specialty-lane reps. Never to commercial-lane reps.

bends._read_me: Bends only happen when an appointment would otherwise have nobody (no reschedule) or to keep a same-day appointment. Never a 5th sit. New and Coaching reps never bend. Every bend is tagged on the card and needs Richie's OK. Penalties are set higher than any close-chance difference, so the engine never bends just to put a better closer on a lead, only to avoid leaving an appointment with nobody.

last_resort._read_me: If an appointment would still have nobody, New and Coaching reps can go one over their daily max or weekly cap rather than reschedule the homeowner. Flagged for Richie's OK. Set enabled to false to never do this.

hot._read_me: Feed the hot hand. Any rep, new or not, whose close rate on the rolling 30 is at Beast level on enough sits is rated Beast: Beast limits and priority. Stays Beast until he drops below off_below. Day 1 sits count, so a new rep can be hot in his first month. Reps in Hero's Journey training (before Day 16) still get no leads.

forecast._read_me: How many more appointments usually get booked for a day between now and that day, from the last N days of history (appointment set date = Prospect Milestone Date). Shown on the board; the engine does not hold slots open for them yet.

_rules_are_evergreen: No rule names a person. Who gets what comes only from data and settings: close odds learned from each rep's own results, rating from his close rate, hot status, lane, hours, days off and capacity. Any rep with the same numbers and settings is treated the same.
